title: Fit rings to pistons, install pistons and rods

notices.text: File-fit every ring: square each ring in its own bore with a piston and measure the end gap against the piston supplier's spec, not a generic figure. Stagger the ring gaps per the supplier's diagram. Use a TAPERED SLEEVE ring compressor, which is what the cylinder design wants — not a band-type compressor. Protect the rod bolts with hose sleeves so nothing touches the crank or the bore. THE 4-6 TRICK: pistons 4-6 must be fed in through the case access opening with the rods already on the crank. Do a dry practice run, use an alignment tool, and verify EVERY wrist pin circlip with a borescope after installation — a circlip that pops out destroys the engine.

fasteners.name: Connecting rod bolts

stages.label: M9 x 1.25 (12 off): stage 1 20 Nm (15 ft-lb), stage 2 +90 deg. Oil thread and contact face.

fasteners.note: OPEN: the torque book gives +90 deg for M96.0X and the WSM M96/01 edition gives +90 deg, but a transcription of the factory 3.6 data (workshop-manuals.com, not verified by us) gives +110 deg for M96/03. Settle this against the book page for the rod before assembly. ARP 204-6301 bolts use ARP's procedure.

sources.ref: Knowledge Gruppe, Fastening Specifications 996, p.19 item 11 (M96.0X); WSM Gr.1 Part 1 (M96/01 edition) p.13-31, 1-1
